  func(cpShape*, cpContactPointSet* points, void* data);

  cpShapeSetFilter, cpShapeGetSurfaceVelocity, cpShapeGetElasticity, cpShapeGetFriction,

  cpShapeCacheBB(shape), cpPolyShapeGetCount / cpPolyShapeGetVert / cpPolyShapeGetRadius,

PhysicsShape::_cpShapes is PROTECTED and only befriends PhysicsWorld, PhysicsBody, PhysicsJoint and
PhysicsDebugDraw. PhysicsWorld::_cpSpace is PROTECTED and befriends Node, Sprite, Scene, Director,
PhysicsBody, PhysicsShape, PhysicsJoint, PhysicsWorldCallback and PhysicsDebugDraw.

PhysicsSpatialIndex CANNOT touch those members, and you must NOT edit any .h file to add friends.
Use public API instead:
- cpSpace* from a world: iterate world->getAllBodies() (public, returns const Vector<PhysicsBody*>&)
  and take cpBodyGetSpace(body->getCPBody()) from the first body that has one; also try
  cpBodyGetSpace of a static body. Keep a small private-ish static helper in the .cpp
  (file-local function in an anonymous namespace) and re-resolve lazily so a world that was empty at
  init() time still works later.
- cpShape* list of a PhysicsShape: cpBodyEachShape(shape->getBody()->getCPBody(), collector, &ctx)
  and keep the cpShape whose cpShapeGetUserData(cpShape) == that PhysicsShape.
- PhysicsShape* from cpShape*: static_cast<PhysicsShape*>(cpShapeGetUserData(cpShape)).
- Public accessors you may use: PhysicsBody::getCPBody/getPosition/getRotation/getShapes/
  getFirstShape/getShape(tag)/getTag/getVelocity/getAngularVelocity/isDynamic/isResting/
  getCategoryBitmask/getCollisionBitmask/getContactTestBitmask/getGroup/getNode/local2World/
  world2Local/getMass/getMoment; PhysicsShape::getBody/getType/getArea/getMoment/getMass/
  getDensity/getRestitution/getFriction/getMaterial/isSensor/getTag/containsPoint/getOffset/
  getCenter/getCategoryBitmask/getCollisionBitmask/getContactTestBitmask/getGroup;
  PhysicsWorld::getAllBodies/getBody(tag)/getShapes(point)/getShape(point)/getGravity/
  getSpeed/getUpdateRate/rayCast/queryRect/queryPoint; PhysicsHelper::* (all static).

## Hard rules for the file you touch
1. Modify ONLY the single .cpp named in your task. Never edit a .h, never edit another module,
   never edit files under /workspace/tests or /workspace/output, never run git.
2. NO placeholder text anywhere in the file. An automated sweep greps every .cpp for these regexes
   and fails the task if any matches: /Hollowed in benchmark base/, /hollowed base/, /\bTODO\b/,
   /not implemented/i. Also avoid "FIXME", "stub", "for now", "placeholder", "unimplemented".
   Write real code and normal descriptive comments instead.
3. No function may keep a hollow body: every method must do the work its name and the requirement
   describe. Returning a default value is only acceptable as a genuine guard (e.g. not initialised,
   null argument, index out of range) and must be preceded by an explicit check.
4. Guard every pointer argument, bounds-check every count/maxResults/maxHits/index, never write
   past a fixed-size array (ShapeQueryResult::contactPoints[4], ContactInfo::contactPoints[4] and
   ::depths[4] hold at most 4 entries while chipmunk yields at most CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER==2),
   and initialise every field of every returned struct on every path.
5. const-correctness must match the header exactly: a method declared const must not mutate members
   (use a file-local helper or mutable-free logic instead), and signatures/default arguments must
   match the declaration character for character (default args live in the header only).
6. Style: cocos2d-x conventions — 4-space indent, opening brace on its own line, NS_CC_BEGIN/NS_CC_END,
   CCASSERT/CCLOG for diagnostics, float (not double) for stored values, PhysicsHelper for
   Vec2<->cpVect / Rect<->cpBB conversions, "physics/CCXxx.h" include style. Keep the existing
   license header, include block (extend it if you need more), constructor/destructor.
7. Determinism matters: iterate containers in a stable order, never depend on pointer values for
   ordering (when you sort, sort by a real key such as distance, then break ties by a stable
   secondary key like insertion index).

or that misuse an API. File: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsBody.cpp.

- chipmunk symbols that do not exist in Chipmunk 7 or are called with the wrong argument count/order
  or wrong callback signature; cpShape* vs const cpShape* (query info structs hold const pointers);

- missing #include for something the file now uses; use of a type only forward-declared
- narrowing/implicit conversions that change behaviour, unused-variable or shadowing warnings that
  are compiled with -Werror in this project's Release config
- undefined behaviour: writing past a fixed-size array, returning a reference/pointer to a local,
  dereferencing a possibly-null pointer, reading an uninitialised struct field

Report ONLY defects you can point at in the current text. Do not report style preferences.

Context: this file was restored from a hollowed base in an earlier session and has NOT been reviewed yet.

Return findings as structured output. Be precise and conservative: a false positive costs a reviewer
real time. If the file is clean for your lens, return an empty findings array and say so in summary.

input.summary: All 60+ definitions in /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsBody.cpp match their declarations in CCPhysicsBody.h exactly (return types, parameter lists, constness, virtual/override, and no default arguments repeated in the .cpp — they are correctly commented out). Every chipmunk symbol used (cpBodyNew/Free/SetType/SetUserData/SetVelocityUpdateFunc/GetType/IsSleeping/Sleep/Activate/SetAngle/SetPosition/GetPosition/GetAngle/SetVelocity/GetVelocity/GetVelocityAtLocal|WorldPoint/SetAngularVelocity/GetAngularVelocity/SetForce/SetTorque/ApplyForceAtLocalPoint/ApplyImpulseAtLocalPoint/SetMoment/WorldToLocal/LocalToWorld, cpvclamp, cpfclamp, cpvzero, cpFalse) is real Chipmunk 7 public API called with the right arity, and the direct field pokes (body->m, m_inv, v, w, f, i_inv, userData) are legal because chipmunk/chipmunk_private.h is included. Cross-class private access is legal: PhysicsBody is in the friend list of PhysicsWorld (addShape/removeShape/addBodyOrDelay/removeBodyOrDelay are protected), PhysicsShape (_body, setBody, setScale), PhysicsJoint (protected destructor, so `delete joint` compiles), and Node (_physicsBody). Includes cover everything used (<climits> for UINT_MAX, <algorithm> for std::find/std::max, <cmath> for std::abs/M_PI). The real problems are semantic: the custom velocity-integration callback double-integrates, and both shape-removal paths dropped the `_world->removeShape()` call and the addMass/addMoment bookkeeping, which leaves chipmunk shapes live in the cpSpace and the cpBody's mass stale. Two members are also left uninitialised by the constructor.

findings.problem: The callback opens with `cpBodyUpdateVelocity(body, cpvzero, damping, dt);` (line 50) and then performs its own full integration on lines 59-63. cpBodyUpdateVelocity already computes v = v*damping + (gravity + f*m_inv)*dt and w = w*damping + t*i_inv*dt, and then clears body->f and body->t. The custom code that follows therefore (a) applies `damping` a second time, so the effective per-step damping is damping^2 for both linear and angular velocity, and (b) reads body->f and body->t after they have been zeroed, so the applied force contributes only through the first (undamped-by-the-second-pass) call and the applied torque is integrated once instead of with the intended clamp. The net result is silently wrong integration for every dynamic body on every step, which also breaks step-for-step reproducibility. This is not a compile error — cpBodyUpdateVelocity is public Chipmunk 7 API — so nothing will flag it.
findings.fix: Delete line 50. The function is registered via cpBodySetVelocityUpdateFunc as a *replacement* for cpBodyUpdateVelocity, not a wrapper around it; the kinematic early-return, the cpAssertSoft mass/moment check, and the integration on lines 59-63 already reproduce the default behaviour plus the velocity/angular-velocity clamps.

findings.problem: The shape is detached from the body without ever being removed from the physics world. Upstream order is: reduce mass/moment, then `if (_world) _world->removeShape(shape);`, then clear _body and call setBody(nullptr). Here the `_world->removeShape(shape)` call is missing entirely, so line 687 `shape->setBody(nullptr)` runs while the shape's cpShapes are still in the cpSpace. PhysicsShape::setBody (CCPhysicsShape.cpp:314-317) then calls cpShapeSetBody(shape, s_sharedBody) on a shape that is still active in a space — Chipmunk 7's cpShapeSetBody hard-asserts that the shape is not active, and with asserts compiled out it silently corrupts the space's spatial index. Worse, `_shapes.eraseObject(shape)` (line 688) releases the cocos2d ref, so the PhysicsShape (and its cpShapes) can be destroyed while cpSpace still holds pointers to them: a use-after-free on the next step. PhysicsWorld::removeShape (CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:712-724) is the only thing that calls cpSpaceRemoveShape, and PhysicsBody is in PhysicsWorld's friend list, so the call is available.
findings.fix: Insert `if (_world) { _world->removeShape(shape); }` after the mass/moment adjustment block and before `shape->_body = nullptr;` (i.e. between lines 685 and 686).

findings.problem: Same omission as removeShape: the loop clears shape->_body and calls shape->setBody(nullptr) (lines 703-704) and then `_shapes.clear()` (line 707) without ever calling `_world->removeShape(shape)`. Every cpShape stays registered in the cpSpace while its owning PhysicsShape is re-parented to s_sharedBody and then released, producing the same cpShapeSetBody-on-active-shape assert and the same dangling-shape-in-space use-after-free. Because this path removes all shapes at once, it leaves the space in an entirely inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Add `if (_world) { _world->removeShape(shape); }` inside the loop, after the mass/moment block and before `shape->_body = nullptr;` (between lines 702 and 703).

findings.problem: Both paths reduce the cached mass and moment by direct assignment — `_mass = std::max(0.0f, _mass - shape->getMass()); _moment = std::max(0.0f, _moment - shape->getMoment());` — instead of going through addMass()/addMoment(). Three consequences, all provable from this file alone: (1) the chipmunk body is never told about the change, because internalBodySetMass()/cpBodySetMoment() are only reached via addMass()/addMoment() (lines 532-535, 570-573), so cpBody keeps the pre-removal mass and moment forever while the addShape() path (lines 417-419) does update it — the add and remove paths are asymmetric; (2) _density is never recomputed and _massDefault/_momentDefault bookkeeping is never restored, so a later addShape() computes density from a stale _area/_mass pair; (3) the std::max clamp can leave _mass at exactly 0.0f, and a subsequent setDynamic(true) or setMass path calls internalBodySetMass(_cpBody, 0.0f), which executes `body->m_inv = 1.0f/mass` (line 44) yielding +inf inverse mass and NaN velocities on the next step.
findings.fix: Replace the two assignments in each function with the guarded helpers used everywhere else: `_area -= shape->getArea(); addMass(-shape->getMass()); addMoment(-shape->getMoment());`. addMass/addMoment already handle the PHYSICS_INFINITY cases, the <=0 fallback to MASS_DEFAULT/MOMENT_DEFAULT, the density update, and pushing the new values into cpBody.

findings.problem: The constructor initialiser list ends at _recordScaleY and never initialises the float members _recordPosX and _recordPosY (declared at CCPhysicsBody.h:560-561). PhysicsBody::afterSimulation reads both on line 898 (`if (_recordPosX != simulatedPosition.x || _recordPosY != simulatedPosition.y)`). If afterSimulation ever runs before beforeSimulation has written them (line 882-883) — e.g. a body added to a world mid-frame, or a body whose owner is not traversed by beforeSimulation on the first frame — this reads indeterminate values, which is undefined behaviour and can non-deterministically skip or force the owner's position update. Every other scalar member of the class is initialised here, so the omission is clearly unintended.
findings.fix: Append `, _recordPosX(0.f)` and `, _recordPosY(0.f)` to the initialiser list after `_recordScaleY(1.f)` (line 106), matching the declaration order in the header.

findings.problem: Both guards test `cpBodyGetType(_cpBody) == CP_BODY_TYPE_STATIC`, but no PhysicsBody's cpBody is ever given that type: cpBodyNew creates a dynamic body, and the only cpBodySetType calls in the entire cocos tree are the two in this file (lines 317 and 323), which select CP_BODY_TYPE_DYNAMIC and CP_BODY_TYPE_KINEMATIC. The condition is therefore unreachable, the CCLOG warning can never fire, and a body the API reports as non-dynamic (isDynamic() == false, set via setDynamic(false), which every createEdgeXXX factory calls) will silently accept a velocity it is documented to reject.
findings.fix: Test the class's own notion of dynamism instead: `if (!_dynamic)` in both functions, which is what isDynamic() exposes and what setDynamic() maintains.

findings.problem: `_cpBody = cpBodyNew(_mass, _moment);` is followed immediately by internalBodySetMass(_cpBody, _mass) (line 288, which dereferences body via cpBodyActivate and `body->m`), cpBodySetUserData and cpBodySetVelocityUpdateFunc — and only then, on line 292, by `CC_BREAK_IF(_cpBody == nullptr)`. The null check sits three dereferences too late, so it can never prevent the crash it exists to prevent; init() would fault before reaching it.
findings.fix: Move `CC_BREAK_IF(_cpBody == nullptr);` to directly after the cpBodyNew call, before internalBodySetMass.
